targets.summary: Tier loop reads tiers[i + 1] without bounding i, so the last tier dereferences undefined.
Balance is read before the awaits and written back after, so concurrent ticks lose updates.
await inside forEach is not awaited, so reserve() returns before any stock is decremented.
Loop bound is <= days, so every window contains one extra day.
discount is optional on the row but dereferenced unguarded, throwing for carts with no coupon.
The final attempt's rejection is swallowed, so retry resolves undefined instead of throwing.
settledAt is a nullable TypeORM column, so an unsettled row loads as null rather than undefined, and isSettled() returns true for every unsettled invoice.
The sweep interval started in the constructor is never cleared on destroy, so the timer keeps the process alive after shutdown.
eligible() returns the inactive suppliers, the exact opposite of what its documentation and name promise. No exception is thrown; the caller sends purchase orders to suspended suppliers.
discount is declared optional on CartRow and dereferenced without a guard, while the equally optional lines is guarded one line above.
The loop bound is <= lastPage, so pageBounds returns one more page than the documented ceil(total / pageSize), and the extra page is empty.
modifiedSince filters on createdAt instead of updatedAt, so an incremental sync silently skips every record that was edited after it was created.
Row permits an absent discount, which is dereferenced without a guard.
The directory Map starts empty; get returns undefined for a missing id, then displayName dereferences name.
The wildcard-exported Row contract permits an absent discount, dereferenced without a guard.
couponFor forwards resolveCoupon, which returns undefined; discount dereferences amount.
Reading converts its input to a string; display calls the numeric toFixed method on that string.
detach() passes a new bound function to off(), so the listener from attach() is never removed and messages keep being forwarded.
take() reads the bucket, awaits, then writes a value from that read; concurrent requests spend the same token and exceed capacity.
The sort comparator returns a boolean, never a negative number, so posts are not reliably newest first.
for...in yields string keys, so rank is the string "01", "11", ... instead of the number 1, 2, ...
A rejected ping is never caught: the health flag is never cleared and the rejection is unhandled.
Overlapping interval fetches can resolve out of order; an older result overwrites a newer one.
lastN starts the slice one element early and returns n + 1 visits.

verdicts.reason: On the last tier `tiers[i + 1]` is undefined, so `next.minQuantity` throws a TypeError. Any quote with at least one tier crashes unless an earlier tier matches first.
`lines.forEach(async ...)` isn't awaited. `reserve` returns `{reserved: []}` before any availability check or decrement finishes, and rejections from `repo.decrement` go unhandled.
The loop uses `i <= days`, so `windowDays(start, 7)` returns 8 dates. The file says windows are exclusive-end, so this is off by one.
`row.discount.amount` throws a TypeError when the cart has no discount. `row.lines` is guarded with `|| []` but `discount` is not.
The catch swallows every error and never rethrows after the last attempt. If all attempts fail, `retry` returns undefined instead of failing. The backoff after the final attempt is also wasted.

`settledAt` is a nullable column, which TypeORM returns as null and not undefined. `isSettled()` compares with `!== undefined`, so it returns true for unsettled invoices. `describe()` at line 32 has the same problem and prints ' (null)'.
The `setInterval` handle in `this.sweep` is never cleared. `onModuleDestroy` only clears the map, so the timer leaks and keeps the process alive.
The filter is inverted (`!supplier.active`). It returns only suspended suppliers and excludes active ones, contrary to the doc comment.
`discount` is optional but `row.discount.amount` is dereferenced unguarded. A cart without a discount throws a TypeError.
The loop uses `page <= lastPage`, so it returns ceil(total/pageSize)+1 entries. The last one is an empty page with from == to == total. This contradicts the doc comment.
`modifiedSince` filters on `createdAt`, so records edited after `since` but created earlier are never synced. The doc says it returns every record edited since then.
`Row.discount` is optional (contracts.ts), and `row.discount.amount` throws a TypeError when it is missing.
`directory.get(id)` returns undefined for an unknown id, since it reads from a Map. `.name` on it throws a TypeError.
`Row` re-exports contracts, where `discount` is optional. `row.discount.amount` throws when it is absent.
`couponFor` is `resolveCoupon`, which always returns undefined. `.amount` on it throws a TypeError.
`Reading.value` is a string (`String(value)`), and strings have no `toFixed`. The call throws a TypeError.
`detach` passes a fresh `this.onMessage.bind(this)` to `off`, which is not the function registered in `attach`. The listener is never removed, so messages keep reaching a possibly disposed handler.
The sort comparator returns a boolean, not a number. `false` becomes 0 and `true` becomes 1, so ordering is inconsistent and posts are not reliably sorted newest first.
`for...in` yields string indexes, so `index + 1` is string concatenation. Ranks come out as '01', '11', '21' and not the documented 1-based numbers.
A rejected `client.ping()` is unhandled. `healthy` is never set to false, contrary to the documented behaviour, and the async interval callback produces an unhandled rejection.
`slice(length - n - 1)` returns n+1 items. `lastN(visits, 2)` on 5 visits returns 3.

verdicts.reason: For the last tier, or a single-tier list, tiers[i + 1] is undefined. When quantity >= the last tier's minQuantity and no earlier tier matched, next.minQuantity throws a TypeError.
Tool result was uncertain and not actionable (possible race between the read and the fresh timestamp), so no defect is reported.

reserve() uses forEach with an async callback that is never awaited. It returns { orderId, reserved } with an empty array before any availability check or decrement finishes, and rejections go unhandled.
The loop uses `i <= days`, so windowDays(start, 7) returns 8 dates, and the last one is the exclusive end. Windows are meant to be inclusive-start and exclusive-end, so it should be `i < days`.
Tool result was uncertain and not actionable (row.discount.amount is dereferenced without a guard), so no defect is reported.
After the final failed attempt the catch block sleeps, then the function falls out of the loop and returns undefined. The last error is swallowed and the caller sees success with no value.
settledAt is a nullable column, and TypeORM hydrates NULL as null, not undefined. For an unsettled invoice loaded from the DB, `null !== undefined` is true, so isSettled() wrongly returns true.
The constructor starts a 60s setInterval stored in this.sweep, but onModuleDestroy never calls clearInterval. The timer keeps running and holds the service alive after shutdown.
The filter is inverted: `!supplier.active` keeps only suspended suppliers. Active suppliers are excluded and suspended ones become eligible for purchase orders.
CartRow.discount is optional, but row.discount.amount is dereferenced without a guard. A row with no discount throws a TypeError.
The loop uses `page <= lastPage`, so it produces one page too many. For total=10 and pageSize=5 it yields 3 pages, the last with from=10 and to=10.
modifiedSince is documented to return customers edited after the given instant, but it filters on createdAt. Records modified after `since` but created earlier are omitted from incremental sync.
Row.discount is optional, so for a row without a discount, reading row.discount.amount throws a TypeError.
directory.get returns undefined for an id not in the directory, and `.name` is then read without a guard. Unknown ids throw a TypeError.
Row.discount is optional, so for a valid Row without a discount, row.discount.amount throws a TypeError.
couponFor is typed to return `{ amount: number } | undefined` and always returns undefined. `couponFor(id).amount` throws a TypeError for any id.
Reading.value is a string (String(value)), and strings have no toFixed method. new Reading(7).value.toFixed(2) throws a TypeError instead of returning "7.00".
detach() calls off() with a new this.onMessage.bind(this) function, which is not the listener registered in attach(). Removal never matches, so the handler keeps receiving messages after detach.

take() reads the bucket, awaits, then writes a value derived from the stale read. Two concurrent requests from one client both see the same tokens and both return true, one decrement is lost, and the limiter admits more than `capacity` requests.
The sort comparator returns a boolean (a.publishedAt < b.publishedAt), which coerces to 1 or 0 and is never negative. Posts are not reliably sorted newest first.
`for...in` yields string keys, so `index + 1` is string concatenation. Rank becomes "01", "11", "21" instead of the numbers 1, 2, 3.
The interval callback awaits client.ping() with no try/catch. A failed ping rejects unhandled and never marks the connection unhealthy, so healthy stays true.
Tool result was uncertain and not actionable (possible stale overwrite from overlapping fetches), so no defect is reported.
The slice start is visits.length - n - 1, so it returns n+1 visits. For 5 visits and n=2 it starts at index 2 and returns 3 items instead of the 2 most recent.

verdicts.reason: For the last tier (or a single tier), tiers[i + 1] is undefined, so next.minQuantity throws a TypeError. Any quantity that doesn't match an earlier tier crashes the quote.

The tool's race finding was uncertain and I dismissed it after reading the source. tick() runs sequentially inside one start() loop, and a concurrent tick would need a second start() call that nothing in the file makes.

forEach with an async callback isn't awaited, so reserve() returns { reserved: [] } before any availability check or decrement finishes. Stock is decremented after the reply, and failures become unhandled rejections.
The window is documented as inclusive-start and exclusive-end, but the loop uses i <= days. windowDays(start, 3) therefore returns 4 dates, including the exclusive end date.
When every attempt fails, the catch swallows each error and the function returns undefined instead of throwing the final failure. Callers see a silent success with no result.

TypeORM hydrates a NULL settledAt as null, not undefined. The `!== undefined` check is therefore true for unsettled loaded invoices, so isSettled() wrongly returns true. describe() also appends " (null)" for a null note.
The constructor starts a setInterval sweep, but onModuleDestroy only clears the map and never calls clearInterval. The timer keeps running and keeps the service alive after shutdown.
eligible() filters with `!supplier.active`, which keeps suspended suppliers and drops active ones. This contradicts the doc that suspended suppliers must never appear.
CartRow.discount is optional, but `row.discount.amount` is dereferenced unguarded. A cart with no discount throws a TypeError.
The loop uses `page <= lastPage`, but the doc promises exactly ceil(total/pageSize) entries. For total=10 and pageSize=5 it returns 3 pages, the last with from=10 and to=10 (empty).
modifiedSince is documented to return records edited since the instant, but it filters on createdAt. Records edited after creation are missed, and only newly created ones are synced.
Row.discount is declared optional, so a Row without a discount makes row.discount.amount throw a TypeError on undefined.
directory.get returns rows.get(id), which is undefined for an id not in the Map. .name.toUpperCase() then throws a TypeError for any missing id.
Row.discount is optional, so a Row without a discount makes row.discount.amount throw a TypeError on undefined.
The coupon resolver is typed to return { amount: number } | undefined, and its shown body returns undefined. couponFor(id).amount therefore throws a TypeError.
Reading.value is a string (String(value)), and strings have no toFixed method. Calling .toFixed(2) throws a TypeError on every call.

detach() passes a new this.onMessage.bind(this) to off(), which is not the function registered in attach(). The listener is never removed, so the bridge keeps forwarding to a possibly disposed handler.

take() reads bucket state with await store.get, then writes a derived value with store.set. Concurrent requests for one client both read the same tokens and each write tokens-1, so more than `capacity` requests are allowed.
The sort comparator returns a boolean (true/false becomes 1/0, never negative), so it is not a valid comparator. byNewest does not reliably order posts newest first.
`for...in` yields string indices, so `index + 1` concatenates. The first row gets rank "01" and the tenth "91", instead of 1-based numbers.
If `client.ping()` rejects, the async interval callback throws. `healthy` is never set to false and the rejection goes unhandled, although a failed ping must mark the connection unhealthy.
The slice start is `visits.length - n - 1`, so it returns n+1 visits. With 5 visits and n=2 it returns the last 3, not the 2 most recent.

verdicts.reason: For the last tier or a single-tier list, tiers[i + 1] is undefined, so next.minQuantity throws a TypeError when the quantity reaches the last tier without an earlier match.
The tool marked its race-condition finding uncertain, so it is not reported.

reserve() uses forEach with an async callback that is never awaited. It returns { orderId, reserved } with an empty reserved array before any availability check or decrement completes, and callback errors become unhandled rejections.
The loop uses i <= days, so windowDays(start, 7) returns 8 dates and includes the exclusive end date. It should be i < days.
The tool marked its null-reference finding uncertain, so it is not reported.

When all attempts fail, the catch swallows every error and the function returns undefined instead of throwing the last error, so callers cannot detect failure. The backoff delay is delayMs*i, so the first retry also waits 0ms.

TypeORM loads a NULL settledAt column as null, not undefined, so the `!== undefined` check makes isSettled() return true for unsettled invoices loaded from the database. describe() has the same flaw and prints "(null)" for a null note.

The constructor starts a 60s setInterval stored in this.sweep, but onModuleDestroy only clears the map and never calls clearInterval. The timer keeps running and keeps the process alive after shutdown.
The filter is inverted (`!supplier.active`), so eligible() returns only suspended suppliers and excludes active ones. This contradicts the documented contract that suspended suppliers never appear.
CartRow.discount is optional, but row.discount.amount is dereferenced without a guard. Any cart without a discount throws a TypeError instead of returning totals with a discount of 0.
The loop uses page <= lastPage, which produces one page too many. For total=10 and pageSize=5 it yields 3 pages, the last with from=10 and to=10.

modifiedSince is documented to return records edited after the given instant, but it filters on row.createdAt. Records edited after `since` but created earlier are never returned, so incremental sync misses updates.
Row.discount is optional, so for a row without a discount, row.discount.amount throws a TypeError instead of returning a default.
directory.get returns undefined for an id not in the directory, and `.name` is then read without a guard, throwing a TypeError for unknown ids.
Row.discount is optional, so for a row without a discount, row.discount.amount throws a TypeError.
couponFor returns { amount: number } | undefined, and the shown definition always returns undefined, but `.amount` is read without a check. discount() therefore throws a TypeError.
Reading.value is a string (String(value)), which has no toFixed method. new Reading(7).value.toFixed(2) throws a TypeError instead of returning "7.00".

detach() calls off() with a new this.onMessage.bind(this) function, which is not the listener registered in attach(). The original listener is never removed, so the bridge keeps forwarding to the handler after detach().

take() reads the bucket from the store, awaits, then writes tokens-1 back. Two concurrent requests from one client both read the same state and both write the same value, so both are admitted for one token and the limit is exceeded.
The sort comparator returns a boolean (a.publishedAt < b.publishedAt) instead of a number. It coerces to 1 or 0 and is never negative, so the sort does not reliably order newest first.
`for...in` yields string keys, so `index + 1` concatenates and ranks become "01", "11", "21" instead of numeric 1, 2, 3.

The interval callback awaits client.ping() with no try/catch. A failed ping never marks the connection unhealthy, as the documented contract requires, and instead raises an unhandled promise rejection.
The tool marked its race-condition finding uncertain, so it is not reported.
The slice start is visits.length - n - 1, so it returns n+1 visits. For 5 visits and n=2 it returns 3 items instead of the 2 most recent.

verdicts.reason: For the last tier, `next` is undefined. Any quantity at or above that tier's minQuantity reads `next.minQuantity` and throws a TypeError, so quote() fails for the highest-volume lines.

tick() reads settled payments at line 29, then awaits ledger.write, then calls markSeen with a fresh Date.now(). A payment that settles during those awaits is not in `settled` but is older than the new lastSeenAt. Later ticks skip it, so it is never applied to the ledger. This came back from the tool as uncertain; I read the source and confirmed it.
forEach with an async callback is not awaited. reserve() returns { reserved: [] } before any decrement runs, and any repo error becomes an unhandled rejection.
The window is documented as exclusive-end, but the loop uses `i <= days`. windowDays(start, 3) returns 4 dates, and the last one is the exclusive end, which isWithin rejects.

When every attempt fails, the catch swallows the error and the function returns undefined instead of throwing, so the caller cannot tell failure from success. The backoff also sleeps delayMs*0 = 0 ms after the first failure.

settledAt is a nullable column, and TypeORM hydrates NULL as null, not undefined. For an unsettled invoice loaded from the database, `!== undefined` is true, so isSettled() wrongly returns true. describe() has the same flaw with note and prints ' (null)'.

The constructor starts a setInterval stored in this.sweep, but onModuleDestroy only clears the map and never calls clearInterval. The timer keeps running and holds the service alive after destruction.
eligible() filters with !supplier.active, so it returns only suspended suppliers and drops the active ones. This contradicts the documented rule that suspended suppliers must never appear.
CartRow.discount is optional and lines is defaulted with ?? [], but row.discount.amount is dereferenced without a guard. A cart without a discount throws a TypeError.
The loop uses `page <= lastPage`, but the doc promises exactly ceil(total/pageSize) entries. With total=10 and pageSize=5 it yields 3 pages, the last with from=10, to=10 (empty).
modifiedSince is documented to return records edited since the instant, but it filters on row.createdAt. Records edited after creation are missed, and only newly created ones are returned.
Row.discount is declared optional, so a valid Row without a discount makes row.discount.amount throw a TypeError.
directory.get(id) returns a Map lookup that is undefined for an unknown id, and .name is then dereferenced without a guard, throwing a TypeError.
Row.discount is declared optional, so a valid Row without a discount makes row.discount.amount throw a TypeError.
couponFor is declared to return `{ amount: number } | undefined`, but `.amount` is read without a guard. When no coupon exists for an id, discount() throws a TypeError.
Reading.value is a string (String(value)), and String has no toFixed method, so new Reading(7).value.toFixed(2) throws a TypeError instead of returning '7.00'.
detach() calls off() with a fresh this.onMessage.bind(this), which is not the function registered in attach(). The listener is never removed, and messages keep reaching the handler after detach.

take() reads state with await, then writes tokens-1 after another await, with no atomicity. Concurrent requests for the same client read the same token count and each write tokens-1, so more than `capacity` requests are admitted.
The sort comparator returns a boolean (1 or 0, never negative) instead of a signed number, so posts are not reliably ordered newest first.
`for...in` yields string keys, so `index + 1` concatenates. Ranks come out as "01", "11", "21" instead of the documented 1-based numbers 1, 2, 3.
The interval callback awaits client.ping() with no catch. A failed ping never marks the connection unhealthy as the header requires, so `healthy` stays true, and the rejection goes unhandled.
`visits.length - n - 1` starts the slice one element too early, so lastN(visits, 3) on 5 visits returns 4 visits instead of the 3 most recent.
